mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during tightening periods (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces corporate optimism.
regime_hint: High unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during UNRATE > 6.5% months.

mechanism_narrative: When the HOUST index rises by more than 10% over two consecutive months, it indicates accelerating industrial demand, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly growth > 10% in the current month relative to prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive or are statistically insignificant (p > 0.05) during qualifying HOUST growth periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO above 2% for three consecutive months signals supply-side contraction, which predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 2% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Economic contraction or weak manufacturing output
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from zero during such INDPRO declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL by at least 0.25 percentage points each are interpreted as dual inflation and policy tightening, predicting a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline ≥ 0.25% in the same month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative or are not statistically significant during such dual declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS above 140,000 in a month is interpreted as labor market stress, which precedes a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not negative or not statistically significant during the PAYEMS spike (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 exceeds 12,000 billion chained dollars for two consecutive quarters, it signals robust consumer demand, predicting a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12,000 for two consecutive quarterly periods
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive or not statistically significant during such quarters (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in RSAFS of at least 5% for three months indicates supply-side weakness, which is expected to produce a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors price in recovery.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 5% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Persistent weakness in financial sector supply
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive or not statistically significant during such declines (p > 0.05).
